q: Complete the proverb: 'Ulta chor ___ ko daante'
note: Used when a wrongdoer turns around and scolds the very person he wronged.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Door ke ___ suhaane'
note: Drums sound sweet from far away; things look better from a distance.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Aasmaan se gira, ___ mein atka'
note: Escaping one trouble only to get stuck in another.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Bandar kya jaane ___ ka swaad'
note: Said when someone can't appreciate something valuable.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Ek anaar, sau ___'
note: One pomegranate, a hundred patients: one thing, far too many people wanting it.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Saanp bhi mar jaaye aur ___ bhi na toote'
note: Solving a problem without any loss to yourself.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Jiski laathi, uski ___'
note: Hindi's version of 'might is right'.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Sau sunaar ki, ek ___ ki'
note: A hundred light taps of a goldsmith equal one blow of a blacksmith.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Thotha chana, baaje ___'
note: An empty gram pod rattles loudest, like 'empty vessels make the most noise'.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Oonchi dukaan, ___ pakwaan'
note: A grand shop with bland food: big show, poor quality.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Ghar ka bhedi ___ dhaaye'
note: Refers to Vibhishan, whose inside knowledge helped bring down Ravan's Lanka.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Doodh ka jala ___ bhi phoonk phoonk kar peeta hai'
note: Chhaachh is buttermilk; the English twin is 'once bitten, twice shy'.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Apni gali mein ___ bhi sher hota hai'
note: Everyone acts brave on home turf.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Lalach buri ___ hai'
note: 'Bala' means a calamity or curse, so greed is a curse.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Khoda pahaad, nikla ___'
note: Dug up a mountain and found a mouse: huge effort, tiny result.

q: Complete the saying: 'Der aaye, ___ aaye'
note: Durust means correct or proper: better late than never.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Ek panth, do ___'
note: One trip, two jobs done, like killing two birds with one stone.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Na rahega baans, na bajegi ___'
note: Remove the root cause and the problem disappears for good.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Chor ki daadhi mein ___'
note: A guilty person gives himself away by acting nervous.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Sab dhaan baais ___'
note: A paseri was a five-seer weight; the saying means treating good and bad alike.

q: Complete the saying: 'Ek aur ek ___'
note: One and one side by side make eleven: unity multiplies strength.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Kaam ka na kaaj ka, dushman ___ ka'
note: Mocks a lazy person who does nothing but eat.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Diya tale ___'
note: It's darkest right under the lamp: wrongs happen closest to those who should know.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Honhaar birvaan ke hot ___ paat'
note: A promising sapling shows glossy leaves early: talent shows itself young.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Jahaan chaah, wahaan ___'
note: A near-literal twin of 'Where there's a will, there's a way'.

q: Complete the muhavara: 'Paanchon ungliyan ___ mein'
note: Often extended with 'aur sar kadhai mein' for total good fortune.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Ghoda ghaas se dosti karega to ___ kya?'
note: Business and friendship don't mix: you can't go easy on your source of income.

q: Complete the muhavara: 'Hatheli par ___ ugaana'
note: Mustard can't sprout on a palm: wanting instant results for slow work.

q: Complete the saying: 'Dekhein oont kis ___ baithta hai'
note: Karvat is the side one lies on: let's see which way things turn out.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Ek myaan mein do ___ nahi reh sakti'
note: Two strong rivals can't share one seat of power.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Bakre ki amma kab tak ___ manaayegi'
note: Unavoidable trouble can only be postponed, not escaped.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Idhar kuaan, udhar ___'
note: A well on one side, a ditch on the other: between the devil and the deep sea.

q: Complete the muhavara: 'Dhaak ke ___ paat'
note: Palash (dhaak) leaves always grow in threes: nothing ever changes.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Sar mundaate hi ___ pade'
note: Ole are hailstones: trouble strikes the moment you begin.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Ek to karela, doosra ___ chadha'
note: Bitter gourd climbing a bitter neem tree: bad made worse.

q: Complete: 'Kahin ki eent, kahin ka roda, Bhaanumati ne ___ joda'
note: Kunba means family or clan: a mismatched group cobbled together.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Andher nagari, chaupat ___'
note: Describes a lawless, badly run place; it's also the title of a classic Hindi satire.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Jaisi karni, waisi ___'
note: Hindi's 'as you sow, so shall you reap'.

q: Complete: 'Haathi ke daant khaane ke aur, ___ ke aur'
note: An elephant's tusks are just for show: said of people whose words and deeds differ.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Ghar ki murgi ___ barabar'
note: What we have at home is never valued enough.

q: Complete: 'Ab pachhtaaye hot kya, jab chidiya chug gayi ___'
note: Regret is useless once the birds have eaten the field.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Jal mein reh kar ___ se bair'
note: Magar is a crocodile: don't feud with the powerful you live beside.

q: Complete the muhavara: 'Oont ke munh mein ___'
note: A cumin seed in a camel's mouth: far too little for the need.

q: Complete the muhavara: 'Jis thaali mein khaana, usi mein ___ karna'
note: To betray the very person who feeds or supports you.

q: What is the feminine of 'sher' (lion) in Hindi?
note: Hindi often forms feminines with '-ni', as in mor to morni.

q: What is the feminine of 'raja' in Hindi?
note: Maharaja becomes maharani the same way.

q: What is the vilom (antonym) of the Hindi word 'sukh'?
note: The pair 'sukh-dukh' is also used together to mean life's ups and downs.

q: What is the everyday tadbhav form of the Sanskrit word 'agni' (fire)?
note: Tadbhav words are Sanskrit words reshaped by centuries of everyday speech.

q: What is the everyday tadbhav form of the Sanskrit word 'hast' (hand)?
note: The tatsam form survives in 'hastkala', meaning handicraft.

q: What is the tatsam (Sanskrit) form of the everyday word 'sooraj'?
note: Surya also gives 'Suryavanshi', the solar dynasty of Ram.

q: Give the one-word Hindi term for 'jo sab kuchh jaanta ho' (one who knows everything).
note: Built from 'sarva' (all) and 'gya' (knowing); 'alpagya' means one who knows little.

q: Give the one-word Hindi term for 'jo kabhi na mare' (one who never dies).
note: Its opposite is 'martya', meaning mortal.

q: The doha poet Rahim (Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan) was the son of which regent of the young Akbar?
note: Rahim also translated Babur's memoirs, the Baburnama, into Persian.

q: What was the pen name of Hindi poet Suryakant Tripathi?
note: Nirala means unique; he was a pillar of the Chhayavad movement.

q: Bihari's famous collection of about 700 dohe is known as what?
note: 'Satsai' literally means a collection of seven hundred verses.

q: Which Sufi poet wrote the 16th-century Awadhi epic 'Padmavat'?
note: Its tale of Queen Padmavati of Chittor inspired many later retellings.

q: Who wrote 'Kamayani', the landmark Chhayavad epic about Manu and Shraddha?
note: Prasad was also a noted playwright, known for 'Chandragupta' and 'Skandagupta'.

q: Who wrote 'Raag Darbari', the satirical Hindi novel set in the village of Shivpalganj?
note: It won the Sahitya Akademi Award and remains a sharp satire of small-town officialdom.

q: Who wrote 'Maila Aanchal', the classic regional novel set in rural Bihar?
note: Renu's story 'Mare Gaye Gulfam' became the 1966 Raj Kapoor film 'Teesri Kasam'.

q: Who wrote the Hindi novel 'Gunahon ka Devta'?
note: Bharati also edited the hugely popular Hindi weekly Dharmyug.

q: Who wrote 'Chandrakanta', the Hindi fantasy novel full of magic and ayyars?
note: Legend has it many readers learned Hindi just to read it.

q: What is the name of the collection of Kabir's verses revered by the Kabir Panth?
note: Many of Kabir's verses also appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.

q: Who wrote the patriotic poem 'Pushp ki Abhilasha' (a flower's wish)?
note: In it, the flower wishes to be strewn on the path walked by brave soldiers.

q: Who wrote the poem 'Jhansi ki Rani', with the line 'Khoob ladi mardaani'?
note: It is one of the most recited poems in Hindi school textbooks.

q: Who wrote the satirical Hindi play 'Andher Nagari'?
note: He is often called the father of modern Hindi literature.

q: Which Chhayavad poet, often called the 'modern Meera', wrote 'Yama'?
note: She won the Jnanpith for 'Yama' and wrote much-loved sketches of her pets.

q: Who wrote 'Aapka Bunty', the novel seen through the eyes of a child of divorce?
note: Her story 'Yahi Sach Hai' was adapted into the 1974 film 'Rajnigandha'.

q: Complete the proverb: 'Taali ek haath se nahi ___'
note: Said when both sides share the blame for a quarrel.

q: Whose famous doha begins 'Kaal kare so aaj kar'?
note: It's the Hindi cousin of 'Never put off till tomorrow what you can do today'.

q: Which Indian English word means to move a meeting or event to an earlier time?
note: Coined as the opposite of 'postpone', it's everyday office English across India.

q: Which English word comes from the Hindi 'champo', meaning to press or knead?
note: It first meant a massage; Sake Dean Mahomed's 'shampooing' baths made it fashionable in Brighton.

q: Which English word for a one-storey house comes from the Hindi 'bangla', meaning 'of Bengal'?
note: The style grew out of Bengali cottages adapted by the British.

q: Which English word for a violent criminal comes from the Hindi 'thag', a cheat?
note: It recalls the Thuggee gangs of highway robbers the British suppressed in the 1830s.

q: Which English word for an unstoppable force comes from the name 'Jagannath'?
note: European travellers described the huge Rath Yatra chariots as unstoppable.

q: The word 'chai' ultimately traces back to which language?
note: It reached Hindi via Persian; 'cha' words spread over land, 'tea' words by sea.

q: What does 'Aa bael mujhe maar' mean?
options: To blame others for your mistakes
To work as hard as an ox
note: Literally 'Come, bull, hit me': asking for trouble.

q: What does the muhavara 'Nau do gyarah hona' mean?
note: 'Police ko dekhte hi chor nau do gyarah ho gaya' means the thief fled.

q: What does 'Ghode bech kar sona' mean?
a: To sleep soundly without a care
options: To sleep soundly without a care
note: Like a trader who has sold all his horses and has nothing left to worry about.

q: 'Eid ka chaand hona' is said of someone who…
note: A friend who vanishes for months hears: 'Aap to Eid ka chaand ho gaye!'

q: What does 'Aasteen ka saanp' refer to?
a: A trusted person who betrays you
options: A trusted person who betrays you
note: Aasteen is a sleeve: a snake hidden in your own sleeve.

q: What does 'Lohe ke chane chabaana' mean?
note: Chewing chickpeas made of iron: seriously tough going.

q: What does 'Daal mein kuchh kaala hai' mean?
note: The English equivalent is 'something is fishy'.

q: What does 'Gaagar mein saagar bharna' mean?
a: To say a lot in very few words
options: To say a lot in very few words
note: Fitting an ocean into a pitcher is high praise for compact poetry.

q: 'Chikna ghada' describes someone who…
a: Is unaffected by advice or criticism
options: Is unaffected by advice or criticism
note: Water slides off a greasy pot just as advice slides off them.

q: What does 'Ghaat ghaat ka paani peena' mean?
note: Having drunk from many riverbanks, such a person has seen it all.

q: What does 'Kaan par joon na rengna' mean?
a: To not be bothered at all
options: To not be bothered at all
note: Not even a louse crawling on the ear makes them react.

q: What does 'Doodh ka doodh, paani ka paani' mean?
note: Separating milk from water: justice where each side gets its due.

q: What does 'Goolar ka phool' refer to?
note: The goolar (cluster fig) hides its tiny flowers inside the fruit, so none are seen.

q: When would you say 'Aapke munh mein ghee shakkar'?
a: When you hope someone's words come true
options: When you hope someone's words come true
note: A warm reply to good news or good wishes.

q: What does 'Aankh ka taara' mean?
note: Parents often call a beloved child 'meri aankhon ka taara'.

q: What does 'Bandar baant' refer to?
a: A division where the middleman grabs everything
options: A division where the middleman grabs everything
note: From the tale of a monkey who 'evens out' two cats' bread by eating it.

q: What does 'Chullu bhar paani mein doob marna' mean?
note: Drowning in a palmful of water: so ashamed you can't face anyone.

q: What does 'Aam ke aam, guthliyon ke daam' mean?
options: Paying too much for too little
note: You enjoy the mangoes and still get paid for the seeds.

q: Which English proverb matches 'Ulte baans Bareli ko'?
options: Every cloud has a silver lining
note: Bareilly was famous for bamboo, so taking bamboo there is pointless.

q: Which English idiom matches 'Til ka taad banaana'?
a: Making a mountain out of a molehill
options: Making a mountain out of a molehill
note: Til is a sesame seed; taad is a towering palm tree.

q: Which English idiom matches 'Hawai kile banaana'?
note: Hawai kile literally means forts made of air.

q: Which English proverb matches 'Chor chor mausere bhai'?
a: Birds of a feather flock together
options: Birds of a feather flock together
Two heads are better than one
note: Literally 'thieves are cousins': wrongdoers stick together.

q: Which English proverb matches 'Apna haath jagannath'?
note: Your own hand is as good as divine help, so do the job yourself.

q: Which English proverb matches 'Nau nagad na terah udhaar'?
a: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
options: A penny saved is a penny earned
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
note: Nine in cash beats thirteen on credit.

q: Which Hindi saying matches 'Casting pearls before swine'?
options: Naya nau din, purana sau din
note: Playing a been to a buffalo: wasting refinement on someone who can't value it.

q: Which Hindi saying matches 'A bad workman blames his tools'?
options: Kabhi ghee ghana, kabhi mutthi bhar chana
Naya nau din, purana sau din
note: Can't dance, so blames the crooked courtyard.

q: Which English proverb matches 'Neem hakeem khatra-e-jaan'?
a: A little knowledge is a dangerous thing
options: An apple a day keeps the doctor away
A little knowledge is a dangerous thing
Too many cooks spoil the broth
note: A half-trained healer is a danger to your life.

q: Which English proverb matches 'Jaisa des, waisa bhes'?
a: When in Rome, do as the Romans do
options: Home is where the heart is
East or west, home is best
When in Rome, do as the Romans do
note: Dress the way the land you're in dresses.

q: Which of these is a Hindi term for 'computer'?
note: It is the title of Hindi Wikipedia's article on computers, though everyday speech just says 'computer'.

q: What is the standard Hindi word for 'telephone'?
note: Doorbhaash means 'far speech', just as tele-phone means 'far sound'.

q: Which Hindi word means 'library'?
note: 'Aalay' means abode, so a pustakaalay is a home for books.

q: Which Hindi word means 'hospital'?
note: Chikitsa means medical treatment; everyday Hindi also says 'aspataal'.

q: What is the Hindi word for 'signature'?
note: Hast (hand) + akshar (letter): letters written in your own hand.

q: Which Hindi word means 'satellite'?
note: Grah is a planet and 'upa' means secondary, so the Moon is Earth's upagrah.

q: Which Hindi word is used for 'television'?
note: It means 'far sight', a neat match for tele-vision.

q: Which Hindi word means 'autobiography'?
note: Aatma (self) + katha (story); a jeevani is a biography of someone else.

q: The famously over-formal 'shuddh Hindi' word 'loh-path-gamini' describes which vehicle?
note: Loh (iron) + path (road) + gamini (one that goes); everyday Hindi just says 'rel' or 'railgaadi'.

q: The Hindi word 'chaabi' (key) was borrowed from which language?
note: From Portuguese 'chave'; Portuguese traders left many household words in Hindi.

q: Which of these Hindi words came from Portuguese?
note: From 'armário', the Portuguese word for cupboard.

q: The word 'kitaab' (book) came into Hindi from which language?
note: The same k-t-b root gives 'kaatib' (scribe) and 'maktab' (school).

q: Which Hindi word for 'bucket' comes from the Portuguese 'balde'?
note: Portuguese sailors reached India in 1498 and left dozens of everyday words.

q: Which of these food names did Hindi borrow from Portuguese?
note: Portuguese 'caju' itself came from a Tupi word in Brazil, the cashew's homeland.

q: The Hindi word 'chaaku' (knife) is borrowed from which language?
note: Hindi textbooks list chaaku alongside 'top' (cannon) as Turkish loanwords.

q: The English word 'rickshaw' ultimately comes from which language?
note: From 'jinrikisha', meaning human-powered vehicle.

q: In Persian, what does 'pyjama' literally mean?
note: From 'pai' (leg) and 'jama' (garment); it reached English through India.

q: 'Khaki' comes from a Hindustani and Persian word meaning what?
note: British troops in India began dyeing uniforms khaki in the 1840s.

q: Which of these English words came from Hindi?
note: From Hindi 'loot', plunder; it entered English in the 18th century.

q: Which English word for a small bed comes from the Hindi 'khaat'?
note: A charpai is a woven khaat on four legs.

q: In Hinglish, what is 'timepass'?
a: Something done just to kill time
options: Something done just to kill time
note: Munching roasted peanuts on a slow train is classic timepass.

q: In Indian college slang, what are 'fundae'?
note: Short for 'fundamentals'; a staple of IIT campus slang.

q: What does 'bindaas' mean?
note: Mumbai slang for someone who lives life without fear.

q: What does the Mumbai slang word 'jhakaas' mean?
note: Anil Kapoor made it his signature exclamation.

q: What is a 'chamcha' in Hindi slang?
note: Literally 'spoon'; 'chamchagiri' is the art of flattering the boss.

q: In Indian slang, who is an 'enthu cutlet'?
note: 'Enthu' is short for enthusiasm; the cutlet adds pure desi flavour.

q: Calling someone a 'tubelight' in Indian slang means they are…
note: Old fluorescent tubes flicker for a while before they light up.

q: What does 'paisa vasool' mean?
note: The ultimate compliment for a masala entertainer.

q: In Indian English, a man's 'co-brother' is…
note: Hindi has its own word for this relation: saadhu.

q: What was Oxford Dictionaries' first Hindi Word of the Year, chosen for 2017?
note: It was announced at the Jaipur Literature Festival in January 2018.

q: Which of these Hindi nouns is feminine?
note: It takes feminine forms: 'meri aatma', never 'mera aatma'.

q: Which of these Hindi nouns ending in '-i' is masculine?
note: We say 'haathi aata hai'; its feminine is 'hathini'.

q: Which Hindi noun is always treated as plural?
note: We say 'uske praan bach gaye', never 'praan bach gaya'.

q: 'Maata-pita' is an example of which samaas?
note: In dvandva both parts matter equally, joined by an implied 'aur'.

q: 'Chauraaha' (a crossing of four roads) is which samaas?
note: Dvigu compounds start with a number, like 'navratna' or 'trilok'.

q: 'Vidyaalay' (vidya + aalay) is formed by which sandhi?
note: Aa + aa merge into a single long 'aa'.

q: Which of these is NOT a Hindi word for the sun?
note: Shashi means the moon; Dinkar, 'maker of the day', is the sun.

q: Which Hindi word means both 'hand' and 'tax'?
note: Hence 'kar-kamal' (lotus hands) and 'aaykar' (income tax).

q: In Hindi grammar, 'ksh', 'tr', 'gy' and 'shr' are called what?
note: Each is written as one joined letter built from two consonants.

q: What is the one-word Hindi term for 'one who has no enemy'?
note: It was also the name of a Magadha king who lived in the Buddha's time.

q: 'Bura jo dekhan main chala, bura na milya koye' is a doha by…
note: The doha ends with the poet finding no one worse than himself.

q: The pad 'Maiya mori main nahi maakhan khaayo' was written by…
note: Little Krishna protests to Yashoda that he never stole the butter.

q: 'Daya dharam ka mool hai' begins a well-known doha by…
note: The doha says compassion is the root of dharma and pride the root of sin.

q: 'Agyeya' was the pen name of which Hindi writer?
note: Agyeya means 'the unknowable'; he edited the landmark 'Tar Saptak' anthologies.

q: Rahim's doha 'Rahiman dhaaga prem ka, mat todo chatkaay' warns against what?
note: A snapped thread can be rejoined, but a knot always remains.

q: Kabir's mixed, wandering-saint style of language is often called what?
note: Acharya Ramchandra Shukla used the term for its blend of many dialects.
